5 Nature Stays in

heroSub: Five of Chiang Mai's nature-focused stays that we've reviewed in depth — a real mineral-onsen ryokan on the Mae Rim hills, a homestay in the rice fields of the smallest district, a treehouse deep in the Chiang Dao forest, pine-forest camping in Hot, and a Japanese farm stay in Pong Yaeng. From about ฿100/person to ฿7,000/night.
introH2: 🌿 How many kinds of nature stay does Chiang Mai have, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: A "nature stay" in Chiang Mai doesn't have just one look, and that's what makes choosing more fun than you'd expect — some are real mineral-onsen ryokans perched 1,200 metres up, selling luxury and a soak in mineral water with a mountain view; some are rice-field homestays selling silence and local life for a few thousand baht per person; some are forest treehouses selling adventure and a digital detox; and some are state-run pine-forest campgrounds that start at just a few hundred baht. Plenty of people come to "experience nature" but pick the wrong style of stay, and end up somewhere too far out, or simpler than they can really handle. This article brings together 5 Chiang Mai nature stays we've reviewed in depth, covering the Mae Rim–Pong Yaeng hills, the Chiang Dao forest, the Galyani Vadhana rice fields, and the pine forest of Hot district — every one drawn from reading real guest reviews, telling you the good points and the honest caveats, comparing prices across 3 sites, and with all the booking links you need.
mrtHtml: Most of Chiang Mai's nature stays sit outside the city, so they take more travel planning than an in-town hotel. The closest in this article is Doi Pong Yaeng–Mae Rim (Onsen @ Moncham, Mori Natural Farm), about 45–60 min from the city centre on a winding mountain road — sedans can make it but take care. Chiang Dao (Tree House Hideaway) is about 1.5 hours, and ordinary cars can't reach the final stretch, so most people book a package that includes a transfer. Hot district (Doi Bo Luang FIO) is about 140 km, 2.5–3 hours, and you'll need your own car. The farthest is Galyani Vadhana district (Kratom Klang Na), about 3 hours, with the last stretch on dirt road — best to have the stay come pick you up. Chiang Mai has no metro; around town you can use Grab or a red songthaew, but for the hills you'll want your own car or the stay's transfer service.

entries.name: Onsen @ Moncham
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Pong Yaeng·Mae Rim · 1,200 m up · ~50 min from city

rooms.type: Grand Terrace Suite with Outdoor Onsen

tags: ⛰️ On the hills near Mon Cham
entries.addr: 293 Moo 2, Tambon Pong Yaeng, Mae Rim, Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: If any Chiang Mai nature stay earns the top score in this article, plenty of reviews give it to Onsen @ Moncham — a Japanese-style ryokan up on the hills of Pong Yaeng sub-district, Mae Rim, near the Mon Cham viewpoint, at around 1,200 metres, where the air runs noticeably cooler than in town, sometimes by ten degrees. What sets it apart from the usual Japanese-style stay is that the onsen is genuine natural mineral water from the Pong Yaeng hot spring — the resort says it's rich in copper, magnesium and calcium, not a heated tub — with both communal baths and private in-room baths for rooms that list them. Real reviews talk about the onsen water in very positive terms; many say it helped their muscles unwind after a full day out, and one international review even called the place "the best of Japanese style in Thailand." All 24 rooms go deep on real ryokan detail, many laid with tatami mats and Japanese futons that a lot of guests found more comfortable to sleep on than expected. Another thing reviews praise again and again is the breakfast, which many rate as genuinely five-star, plus the warm service from a small team that looks after everyone closely because there are only 24 rooms. Honest caveats from the reviews: it's up on the hills, far from town, so you should budget nearly an hour each way; the winding road gets slippery in the rainy season with heavy fog; dining options outside the resort are few, so you'll mostly rely on the resort kitchen; and the in-room onsen baths come only with certain room types, so pick the right room name. This is the best-value pick for couples and for anyone who wants a slower-paced getaway, a soak in the onsen with a mountain view, and a resort that's the destination of the trip in itself.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you want a private onsen with a view, choose a room in the Outdoor Onsen or Onsen Suite group, since not every room has an in-room bath. Budget extra time for the drive up, and if you're not driving yourself, book the resort transfer in advance. Bring a warm jacket, because mornings and nights up here really are cold.
pros: Genuine natural mineral onsen from the Pong Yaeng source, scoring 9.6 — the highest in this article
Detailed Japanese atmosphere, tatami rooms, comfortable futons
Cool air at 1,200 metres up, full Mae Rim mountain views
Warm service from a small team, attentive because there are only 24 rooms
cons: Up on the hills, far from town — budget about an hour each way
Few dining options outside the resort, so you rely on the resort kitchen
In-room onsen baths only come with certain room types — pick the right room name

entries.name: Kratom Klang Na
entries.badge: 🌾 Lots of reviews · best value for the experience
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Galyani Vadhana · ~3 hrs · dirt road at the end
entries.addr: Tambon Mae Daet, Galyani Vadhana District, Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: Kratom Klang Na is a stay that's hard to describe by hotel standards, because it isn't a hotel — it's a bamboo homestay set among terraced rice fields in Mae Daet sub-district, Galyani Vadhana, one of the newest and smallest districts in Chiang Mai. Among the nature stays we've reviewed, this one has a fairly large pile of reviews, around 120, scoring about 9.4. What people talk about most is the large windows that open onto rice fields at almost 360 degrees — lying in bed you can see the rice swaying in the wind, and nearly every real review agrees that the first feeling on arrival is "so quiet you can hear yourself breathe." Another draw is the roughly 1,200-baht-per-person package that includes several home-cooked meals from the hosts and a transfer for the final 10 km of dirt road; many reviews call it great value compared with staying at an in-town resort where you'd pay for meals separately and not get a view like this. Dinner by the campfire in the cool air under a sky full of stars is an image that recurs across many reviews, and the hosts' friendliness leaves a lot of guests feeling like they're staying at a relative's house. Honest caveats from the reviews: it's a long trip, about 3 hours, and the final 10 km is dirt road climbing into the hills, so sedans and low-clearance cars struggle to make it themselves and you'll need the transfer; phone signal is limited and some networks barely work; the stay is simple with no air-conditioning; and the view depends heavily on the season — come at the wrong time and the fields may not be green. Book via Facebook or by phone directly; there's no automated online booking. It suits couples and groups of friends who want serious slow-life, with the stay as the destination of the trip.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Match the season to the view you want — around Jul–Oct the fields are fresh green, and around Nov the rice turns golden and the sea of mist begins. Book ahead through the "Kratom Klang Na" page or by phone, since there's no online booking system. Don't force a low-clearance car up yourself — have the stay come pick you up and ask about road conditions first.
pros: 360-degree rice-field-view rooms, a calm you can't find in the city
Around ฿1,200/person including several meals and the final-stretch transfer — great value
Nighttime campfire and a sky full of stars — many call it the most healing part
Friendly, attentive hosts — like staying at a relative's house
cons: Long trip, about 3 hours, with the final 10 km on dirt road
Limited phone signal — some networks barely have any
Very simple, no air-conditioning · view depends on the season · must book via FB/phone

entries.type: Eco Tree House Lodge · treehouse in the forest
entries.name: Tree House Hideaway
entries.revCount: TripAdvisor 4.8/5 · 64 reviews · #1 of 33 Chiang Dao stays
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chiang Dao·in the forest · ~1.5 hrs · ordinary cars can't reach
entries.addr: Mae Mae Village, Mae Na, Chiang Dao District, Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: Tree House Hideaway isn't a hotel as we know it — it's an eco-lodge built as a treehouse from bamboo and timber, set in Mae Mae village, Mae Na sub-district, Chiang Dao, about 1.5 hours north of the city centre. On the review platforms it holds TripAdvisor 4.8/5 and ranks #1 of 33 specialty stays in Chiang Dao from 64 reviews. The heart of the place is the big main treehouse with 4 bedrooms and a large shared deck looking out over forest and a stream, while anyone wanting more privacy can take a separate cabin in the forest. The concept is clear from the name — "Hideaway" means a place to hide away, and that's exactly what it does: the treehouse deliberately has no Wi-Fi and no air-conditioning, just a mosquito net, a fan, the sound of running water, and a sky full of stars. Many reviews say it felt strange at first to put the phone down, but after a few hours they found they really did rest their minds. The real strength is the "experience" more than the "room" — most packages come with a licensed guide who takes you trekking to waterfalls, touring the Chiang Dao cave, soaking in hot springs, ziplining and rafting. Food is another point reviews single out, served as a freshly made Thai–Northern buffet, and many say dinner was one of the best meals of their Thailand trip. Team members like Arty, Mr. Moo and Arm get named in reviews as cheerful and attentive. Honest caveats from the reviews: it's a long trip, about 1.5 hours, and ordinary cars can't reach the final stretch so you cross the stream on foot; bathrooms are small and getting old; there are ants and spiders, natural to the forest; the power cuts out at times; and some drinks cost extra. It suits nature lovers, adventurous families, and couples who want to escape the city into the forest for 1–2 nights.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Booking a package that includes a transfer from the city/airport is the most convenient and best value, since the way in is far and ordinary cars can't reach it. Pack strong mosquito/insect repellent, a flashlight, and a warm jacket. If you have dietary restrictions, make them clear well ahead, as some reviews ran into trouble adjusting the menu.
pros: A rare treehouse-in-the-forest atmosphere, sleeping to the sound of the stream
Licensed guides lead waterfall and Chiang Dao cave treks well — warm and caring
Freshly made Northern-Thai buffet — many reviews call it the tastiest of the trip
A real digital detox · TripAdvisor #1 of 33 Chiang Dao stays
cons: Long trip, ~1.5 hours, with ordinary cars unable to reach the final stretch
Small, aging bathrooms, occasional power cuts, insects natural to the forest
No air-conditioning/Wi-Fi in the treehouse · some drinks cost extra

entries.type: FIO forest-park stay · camping & wooden cabins
entries.name: Doi Bo Luang FIO Forest Park
entries.badge: 🌲 Pine forest · starts at just a few hundred baht
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Bo Luang·Hot district · ~140 km · own car required
entries.addr: Doi Bo Luang FIO Forest Park, Tambon Bo Luang, Hot District, Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: Doi Bo Luang FIO is a stay that's hard to describe by ordinary hotel standards, because it's neither a hotel nor a resort — it's a forest park managed by the Forest Industry Organization (FIO), which opens part of it to visitors to stay among rows of pines planted over 30 years ago, in Bo Luang sub-district, Hot, in the southern part of Chiang Mai. Among the nature stays we've reviewed, this one has the most reviews, around 240. The real selling point isn't the furniture or the facilities but the "atmosphere" — rows of tall pines lined up so neatly that many people's photos look like they were taken abroad, cool comfortable air almost year-round, and morning mist drifting between the trees; a lot of reviews use the phrase "like slipping into another world." There are several types of stay for different budgets and styles, from the triangle-roofed A-frame cabins (the most popular and hardest to book), pine-row cabins, twin cabins, caravans and bare-concrete cabins, all the way to 3 camping grounds that hold over 50 tents for an upkeep fee of only about 100 baht per person — and walk-ins are welcome with no advance booking, unlike the cabins, which must be booked online. Averaged per person it's far cheaper than many similar nature stays in Chiang Mai. Honest caveats from the reviews: the location is very far, about 140 km, a 2.5–3 hour drive up into the hills, and you'll need your own car since there's no public transport that goes all the way; the popular A-frame cabins are hard to book and fill fast in high season; facilities and food options are limited so you should bring your own supplies; and cabins are booked only through chiangmaifio.com — no phone or Facebook bookings. It suits campers, families, and nature lovers who like things simple and want a pine-forest atmosphere at a price you can reach.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Cabins are booked only through chiangmaifio.com; A-frame cabins fill fast in the cool season, so book well ahead, while the campground takes walk-ins. Bring a warm jacket in every season, because nights and mornings really are cold. Buy supplies, food and drinking water in Hot town before heading up the hill, and check your car and fill the tank.
pros: A pine-forest atmosphere as pretty as somewhere abroad, cool air year-round
Beautiful morning mist, especially in the rainy and cool seasons
Friendly prices — tents around 100 baht/person, cabins from about ฿1,000/unit
Several types of stay + 3 camping grounds that take walk-ins, no booking needed
cons: Very far from the city, ~140 km, a 2.5–3 hour drive up into the hills
Own car required · popular A-frame cabins hard to book, fill fast
Limited facilities/food · cabins booked online only

entries.name: Mori Natural Farm
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Pong Yaeng·Mae Rim · near Mon Cham · ~45 min from city
entries.addr: 88/9 Moo 3, Ban Muang Kham, Tambon Pong Yaeng, Mae Rim, Chiang Mai
entries.storyHtml: Mori Natural Farm isn't an in-town hotel and isn't a five-figure luxury resort — it's a small farm stay that the owner family deliberately built up on the hills of Pong Yaeng sub-district, Mae Rim, in the same zone as Mon Cham. The word "Mori" (森) in Japanese means "forest," which captures the concept exactly — a handful of houses tucked among an organic vegetable garden, trees and mountains. What sets Mori apart from the usual hill stay is how it blends a Japanese feel with a Lanna garden-house style seamlessly, not just slapping a "Japanese" label on it but going into detail, from the hot bath and yukata sets to a Japanese-style breakfast made from the farm's own produce. The heart of it is just 4 private houses — the Ryokan House, a rice-barn house that reinterprets the Lanna granary in a new way, the Cottage House and the Wabi-Sabi House — each with a large hot bath that many guests call the star: a warm soak in the evening once the hill air turns cool, then a change into a yukata for a stroll in the garden. Real reviews mention a friendliness like staying at a relative's house, and the one thing you can't leave out is the Akita dog that acts like the host, welcoming guests — a signature that makes the place memorable. The freshly made Japanese breakfast, like rice topped with grilled saba, also draws repeat praise. Honest caveats from the reviews: it's up on the hills, about 45 minutes from town; the path from the car park up to the houses is steep, hard for older guests or anyone with heavy luggage; each house is on the small side, cosy and compact; dining options outside the farm are few; and you should understand that the baths here are in-room warm water, not a natural mineral onsen. It suits couples, nature lovers, and anyone who wants a Japanese atmosphere on a reachable budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're after a real mineral onsen, look at Onsen @ Moncham in this article instead, since Mori's are in-room warm-water baths. Ask about the steep path up to the houses beforehand if you're coming with older guests or heavy luggage. With only 4 houses, book several weeks ahead for high season and long weekends — and don't miss the Japanese breakfast.
pros: Japanese–Lanna concept done with real detail, just 4 private houses
In-room hot bath and yukata sets — a ryokan feel on a budget
Freshly made Japanese breakfast from the garden, praised for being tasty
Friendly, like staying at a relative's house, with an Akita dog to welcome you
cons: Up on the hills, far from town — budget 40–60 minutes each way
Steep path from the car park up to the houses, hard for older guests
The baths are in-room warm water, not a natural mineral onsen

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates from the standard room/package range and may change by date and season; we recommend checking the real price and comparing several channels before every booking. The scores and highlights in this article come from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms and social media — we did not stay ourselves. Some nature stays don't take bookings through the usual Agoda/Booking — Doi Bo Luang FIO books cabins only through chiangmaifio.com (the campground takes walk-ins), while Kratom Klang Na is booked via Facebook or by phone directly. Stays on the hills and in the forest are cooler than in the city, so bring a warm jacket in every season and plan your travel to arrive before dark. In the cool season (Nov–Feb) and on long weekends rooms fill fast, so book ahead. Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — questions travellers often ask about Chiang Mai nature stays

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best nature stay in Chiang Mai?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style. By score and luxury, Onsen @ Moncham scores 9.6, the highest in this article — a real mineral-onsen ryokan on the Mae Rim hills. For the best-value slow-life, Kratom Klang Na, a rice-field homestay with meals included. For the adventurous, Tree House Hideaway, a treehouse in the Chiang Dao forest, TripAdvisor #1. For budget camping, Doi Bo Luang FIO. And for a Japanese atmosphere, Mori Natural Farm.

faq.q: ❓ How much do Chiang Mai nature stays cost?
faq.a: In this article the starting prices range widely, from camping at around ฿100/person at Doi Bo Luang FIO up to ฿7,000/night and above at Onsen @ Moncham. The easy-to-reach end is Kratom Klang Na at around ฿1,200/person with meals, and Tree House Hideaway from ฿1,500/night. Mid-range is Mori Natural Farm from ฿3,300/house. All prices are approximate starting rates; during festivals and the cool season they may run higher than usual.

faq.q: ❓ How do you get to most Chiang Mai nature stays, and are they far?
faq.a: Most sit outside the city. The closest is the Pong Yaeng–Mae Rim zone (Onsen @ Moncham, Mori Natural Farm), about 45–60 minutes. Chiang Dao (Tree House Hideaway) is about 1.5 hours, with ordinary cars unable to reach the final stretch. Hot district (Doi Bo Luang FIO) is about 140 km, 2.5–3 hours. And the farthest, Galyani Vadhana (Kratom Klang Na), is about 3 hours with the last stretch on dirt road. For the hills you'll want your own car or the stay's transfer service.

faq.q: ❓ Which Chiang Mai nature stay has a real mineral onsen?
faq.a: In this article there's only one with a genuine natural mineral onsen: Onsen @ Moncham, which uses water from the Pong Yaeng hot spring. Mori Natural Farm has an in-room Japanese-style warm-water bath, not a mineral onsen — if you want real mineral water, choose Onsen @ Moncham. The others in this article focus more on forest, rice-field and stream atmosphere than on a mineral soak.

faq.q: ❓ Which Chiang Mai nature stay suits couples / families / campers?
faq.a: Couples suit Onsen @ Moncham (an onsen with a mountain view) and Mori Natural Farm (private, 4 houses). Families and the adventurous suit Tree House Hideaway (a full set of forest-trek activities). Campers suit Doi Bo Luang FIO (3 camping grounds, walk-ins welcome). And Kratom Klang Na suits both couples and groups of friends who want quiet slow-life.

faq.q: ❓ How do you book a Chiang Mai nature stay, and do you need to book ahead?
faq.a: Most stays in this article are small (some just 4 houses, or 24 rooms), so they fill fast. Onsen @ Moncham and Mori Natural Farm can be booked through Agoda/Booking/Trip.com. Doi Bo Luang FIO books cabins only through chiangmaifio.com (the campground takes walk-ins). Kratom Klang Na is booked via Facebook or by phone directly. In the cool season (Nov–Feb) and on long weekends, book several weeks to 1–2 months ahead.
